title: holdback-drain-coordinator: gentle-drain prober and KV-dilution guard for continuous-batcher
author: Diego Ramos
description:
Motivation: Continuous-batcher performance regressions were observed in mixed KV-heavy and short-tail workloads: aggressive slot holdback + KV pinning caused starvation of small low-cost requests and elevated 99.9th percentiles during sustained bursts. This PR introduces a coordinator that performs gentle, probe-driven holdback draining and a KV-dilution guard that prevents long-lived KV pins from blocking drain progress.

Design summary: 1) Holdback Drain Coordinator: a light-weight control loop that emits periodic drain probes to candidate queue slots. Drains are 'gentle' — probes request a small targeted reclaim window rather than full preemption, allowing in-flight KV work to finish when safe. 2) Probe-driven slot reclaim: probes carry a reclamation budget and backoff jitter; when a probe is accepted, the slot performs a bounded, cooperative drain sequence with best-effort KV cache checkpointing hints. 3) KV-dilution guard: tag slots with recent-KV-activity scores and delay hard reclaim if the activity score exceeds a threshold; instead, coordinator retries with exponential backoff and incremental budget increases. 4) Timeout smoothing: replace abrupt deadline evictions with a smoothed probability-based eviction that respects workload priorities (latency-sensitive vs batch-y).

What changed (high level): - runtime/scheduler/holdback_coordinator.{h,cc}: new coordinator loop, probe and budget structs, tuning knobs. - runtime/scheduler/kv_activity_tracker.{h,cc}: track KV touch rates per slot and expose dilution_score API. - runtime/scheduler/slot_reclaimer.cc: implement cooperative drain path used by probes, with lightweight checkpointing hint emission. - runtime/config/defaults.yaml: new knobs (holdback_probe_interval_ms, probe_budget_tokens, kv_dilution_threshold). - tests/scheduler/holdback_drain_test.cc: unit + integration tests exercising drain success/fail/backoff paths. - docs/operational/holdback-drain.md: runbook and recommended tuning for dedicated vs hosted deployments.

Testing and results: Microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 serving cluster with mixed workload (70% short text generation, 30% KV-intensive rerank) show: - 99.9th latency for short requests decreased by ~11% (from 142ms to 126ms) under sustained load. - Median latency unchanged within noise. - Overall throughput preserved; observed transient CPU on scheduler thread increased ~6% but remained under budget. - Cost impact: negligible (estimated +0.4% CPU billing).

Safety and rollout: Feature gated behind runtime flag (holdback_drain_coordinator.enabled=false by default). rollout plan: enable in internal canary fleet for 72h, monitor 99/99.9 latency and KV eviction metrics, then ramp to 20% in hosted, and offer as default for Dedicated with ops approval.

Backwards compatibility: no user-facing API changes. Config knobs added with conservative defaults. No breaking change expected.

Notes: This PR avoids heavy-weight preemption and instead uses cooperative reclaim to reduce spoofed evictions and tail amplification caused by KV pin churn. See docs/operational/holdback-drain.md for tuning guidance.

review_comments:
Maya Chen: Can you show proof that KV-dilution threshold doesn't regress throughput in KV-heavy-only workloads? Suggest adding a microbenchmark in CI that runs pure KV pin workload.
Author (Diego): added a KV-only microbenchmark in tests/scheduler/kv_dilution_bench.cc and linked the results in the doc.

Oliver Grant: The exponential backoff tuning looks aggressive — on some runs we saw reclaim delays of several seconds. Suggest capping max backoff and adding jitter to avoid synchronized retries.
Author (Diego): capped max_backoff at 750ms and added per-coordinator jitter; updated unit tests to assert backoff bounds.

Priya Nair: Add observability: expose metrics for probe_success_rate, avg_drain_time, kv_dilution_retries.
Author (Diego): added metrics: scheduler.holdback.probe_success_total, scheduler.holdback.avg_drain_ms, scheduler.kv.dilution_retries_total; wire-up in docs and dashboards.

Maya Chen: CI flaky on holdback_drain_test on macOS runner, likely due to real-time timers — please make timers testable via injected clock.
Author (Diego): refactored coordinator to accept Clock interface in tests and stabilized flaky test; CI green after rerun.
Oliver Grant: LGTM after CI fixes and metric additions.
release_notes: Introduce holdback drain coordinator and KV-dilution guard to improve continuous-batcher tail latency in mixed KV workloads. Feature is off by default; ops rollout recommended. See docs/operational/holdback-drain.md for tuning.
